fr.title: GGC - Freshmen admission (never attended college): GPA, test-optional policy, codes

tuit.title: GGC - Undergraduate tuition and fees (Fall 2026 through Summer 2027)

test_policy.notes: GGC is test-optional for admission. Freshmen need a 2.00 GPA recalculated on the 17 units of the Required High School Curriculum; international applicants need the same 2.00 GPA shown on a NACES or InCred credential evaluation. Scores may be required for scholarship consideration and are recommended for English and math placement (without them, students may be placed into corequisite learning support).

requirements.notes: Apply by creating a Grizzly Profile; $30 non-refundable fee. Freshmen send an official document-by-document credential evaluation (including GPA) from a NACES member or InCred to the evaluator, not foreign transcripts to GGC. After admission, F-1 students must show a bank statement or bank letter covering one academic year of expenses (sponsors also sign an Affidavit of Financial Support). Essays and recommendations are not mentioned.

deadlines.label: Priority application deadline, fall semester (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The Priority tab of the deadlines page lists Fall May 1, Spring Nov. 1, Summer April 1 (no year printed, so fall 2027 is assumed). The Regular tab currently shows only Spring 2027 (applications Dec. 1, documents Dec. 15); a regular fall 2027 date is not yet published. Applications are open for Spring, Summer and Fall 2027. Dates may be extended.

deadlines.label: International out-of-state tuition waiver application window closes
deadlines.notes: Window runs April 1 to July 1; a second window runs Oct. 1 to Dec. 15. The page does not say which term each window covers. Competitive, limited and not guaranteed. The year is not printed, so 2027 is assumed.

english_policy.waiver_notes: International applicants must show English proficiency (see the University System of Georgia English Proficiency Chart for approved exams). Placement into college-level English without a co-requisite on Next Gen ACCUPLACER (Reading Comprehension 237 and WritePlacer 4) waives the requirement; transfer students with English 1101 or 1102 at a C or better from a US accredited institution may also be waived. The GGC page lists only TOEFL iBT and IELTS minimums and does not mention Duolingo, PTE, Cambridge or a conditional-admission/ESL pathway.

english.notes: Listed as 'TOEFL IBT 69'; no new 1-6 scale value is given.

cost.notes: Tuition page (Fall 2026 to Summer 2027), flat rate for 15+ credits per semester, doubled for two semesters: in-state $2,070, out-of-state $8,280, out-of-country $8,520 per semester. Mandatory fees are the sum of the listed per-semester fees ($622) doubled; the cost-of-attendance page shows tuition plus mandatory fees of $17,814 for out-of-state residents (it is not specific to out-of-country tuition). Housing and meals $15,810 (on campus), books $1,670, miscellaneous $3,080; transportation $2,880 is not included in other costs. Total cost of attendance for out-of-country students is not published

aid.notes: F-1 students can apply to International Student and Scholar Services for an international out-of-state tuition waiver: limited, highly competitive, not guaranteed, judged on demonstrated financial need, essay quality and community service. The amount of the waiver is not published. Test scores may be required for other scholarships; no international merit scholarship is described.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the reviewed pages.
